items.title: Nasdaq futures lead ahead of central bank speakers.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down the morning's market action as stock futures trade higher, led by the Nasdaq. Treasury yields move slightly higher while the U.S. dollar drops, providing a lift to gold, silver, and copper. Crude oil prices fall below $88. Focus shifts to a slate of central bank speakers over the next 24 hours, including Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller and Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey. The latest U.S. CPI report remains a key driver for inflation expectations. Plus, a look at earnings from companies with market caps over $1 billion and upcoming economic data from Australia and China.

items.title: European defence stocks under fire: is the long-term investment case changing?
items.excerpt: Key takeaways US political uncertainty and Rheinmetall's weaker outlook have exposed growing doubts about defence companies' ambitious growth expectations. Europe's rearmament remains a structural priority , supported by rising military budgets and long-term security needs. Investors should focus on valuations, contract execution and cash generation rather than spending promises alone. After years of enthusiasm surrounding Europe's rearmament, the sector has come under renewed pressure. The Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections has raised questions about future American military spending, while Germany's Rheinmetall has disappointed investors with another reduction to its annual outlook. items.title: Investor Q&A: Panic, buying opportunity or time to rethink portfolios?
items.excerpt: What happened in markets? Wall Street suffered its sharpest selloff in months on 5 November. The Nasdaq 100 plunged 6.4%, wiping out around $2.5 trillion in market value, while the S P 500 declined 4.4% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 12.2%. The selling spread into Asia, particularly the semiconductor-heavy markets of South Korea, Taiwan and Japan. But the weakness was not universal. US Treasuries rallied: Investors sought safety amid concerns about growth and a potential slowdown in AI investment, pushing yields lower. Gold's performance was mixed: Lower yields and policy uncertainty provided potential support, but liquidity-driven selling can also weigh on gold as investors raise cash. items.title: British Pound futures pull back from 1.35 after Bank of England rate hike.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures retreated after touching the 1.35 level early in the session, closing near 1.3450. Volatility in the currency continues to trend lower following the Bank of England's decision to raise interest rates by 25 basis points to 4%. Markets are now weighing the central bank's signals that further rate hikes remain possible before the end of the year, contrasting with the Federal Reserve's recent posture.

items.title: British Pound futures rally as Bank of England decision approaches.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures extended their advance for a sixth consecutive day, gaining 2.1% over the last 14 sessions as traders positioned ahead of the Bank of England's rate decision. Markets broadly anticipate the central bank to hike rates to 4%, with an additional 100 bps of increases priced in over the next year. Meanwhile, the U.S. Dollar Index traded lower following election results, as a divided Washington shifted the outlook for government spending and potential stimulus, weighing on Treasury yields and reducing the dollar's interest rate advantage.

items.title: Australian Dollar futures hit 2.5-week low after RBA rate hike.
items.excerpt: Australian Dollar futures fell for a second consecutive session, dropping 0.5% to 0.6960 and hitting a two-and-a-half-week low. The selling pressure follows the Reserve Bank of Australia's decision to raise interest rates by 25 basis points. Despite the hike, three dissenting officials voted to hold rates, and the central bank issued dovish forward guidance, pushing the Aussie dollar toward the lower end of its recent two-month range. Meanwhile, the broader FX market saw mixed action, with the euro and British pound trading slightly higher.
